text:
**Deep-subprime** had the highest average 30-day delinquency in 2026, at about **5.45%**. That's roughly 1.6 times Subprime (3.37%) and close to 10 times Prime (0.57%).

The 2026 data only covers the months ending January 31 to June 30, so this is a first-half figure, not a full year.
sql:
WITH __ms AS (
  SELECT
    credit_tier,
    month_end,
    YEAR(month_end) AS report_year,
    delinquency_rate_30d
  FROM SNOWPACK_MACRO_STRESS.CORE.MACRO_STRESS_BENCHMARK
)
SELECT
  credit_tier,
  AVG(delinquency_rate_30d) AS avg_delinquency_30d,
  MIN(month_end) AS start_month,
  MAX(month_end) AS end_month
FROM __ms
WHERE
  report_year = 2026
GROUP BY
  credit_tier
ORDER BY
  avg_delinquency_30d DESC NULLS LAST /* Generated by Cortex */;

text:
Over the last two holiday seasons, transaction volume and consumer sentiment went in opposite directions. Volume went up while sentiment went down.





- **Volume rose:** Nov–Dec 2025 volume was about $12.32B, up roughly 5.4% from about $11.69B in Nov–Dec 2024. November 2025 was about $6.18B, around 6.0% above November 2024. December 2025 was about $6.14B, around 4.8% above December 2024.
- **Sentiment fell:** Average consumer sentiment dropped about 5 points, from roughly 70.0 in the 2024 season (69.92 in November, 69.99 in December) to roughly 64.9 in 2025 (64.56 in November, 65.27 in December).
- **What it means:** With only four months of data, there's no positive link between sentiment and spending here. Weaker sentiment didn't hold back holiday volume.
- **Within each season:** Volume was nearly flat from November to December. In 2025, December was slightly below November even though sentiment ticked up a little.

The data has no Nov–Dec 2026 months yet, so the 2026 season isn't included.
sql:
WITH __ms AS (
  SELECT
    is_holiday_season,
    month_end,
    consumer_sentiment,
    transaction_volume_usd
  FROM SNOWPACK_MACRO_STRESS.CORE.MACRO_STRESS_BENCHMARK
)
SELECT
  month_end,
  SUM(transaction_volume_usd) / NULLIF(1e9, 0) AS volume_usd_b,
  AVG(consumer_sentiment) AS avg_consumer_sentiment,
  COUNT(*) AS n_rows
FROM __ms
WHERE
  is_holiday_season = TRUE
GROUP BY
  month_end
ORDER BY
  month_end /* Generated by Cortex */;
question: How did holiday-season (Nov-Dec) transaction volume track against consumer sentiment over the last two years?

text:
BNPL volume fell by about 29–31% in every credit tier from December 2025 to June 2026. All four tiers combined went from about $874M to $614M, a drop of roughly $260M.





- **Subprime** fell the most in percentage terms, down 31.2% ($239M → $165M).
- **Near-prime** fell the most in dollars, down $82M or 29.2% ($281M → $199M). It's still the largest tier.
- **Prime** fell 29.3% ($245M → $173M).
- **Deep-subprime** fell the least in percentage terms, down 29.0% ($109M → $78M).

The declines are very close together across tiers, so they look like one portfolio-wide drop rather than a problem in a particular risk tier. December is a holiday month in this data, so comparing it with June probably shows the normal seasonal decline more than any credit-driven change. To isolate the trend, you could compare June 2026 with June 2025, or look at the months in between.
sql:
WITH __ms AS (
  SELECT
    credit_tier,
    month_end,
    product,
    transaction_volume_usd
  FROM SNOWPACK_MACRO_STRESS.CORE.MACRO_STRESS_BENCHMARK
), b AS (
  SELECT
    credit_tier,
    month_end,
    SUM(transaction_volume_usd) AS v
  FROM __ms
  WHERE
    product ILIKE '%BNPL%' AND month_end IN ('2025-12-31', '2026-06-30')
  GROUP BY
    1,
    2
)
SELECT
  c.credit_tier,
  p.v AS dec_2025_volume,
  c.v AS jun_2026_volume,
  c.v - p.v AS change_usd,
  (
    c.v - p.v
  ) / NULLIF(NULLIF(p.v, 0), 0) AS pct_change
FROM b AS c
LEFT JOIN b AS p
  ON c.credit_tier = p.credit_tier AND p.month_end = '2025-12-31'
WHERE
  c.month_end = '2026-06-30'
ORDER BY
  pct_change /* Generated by Cortex */;

text:
Charge-off rates rose in every credit tier from Q3 2025 (Jul–Sep 2025) to Q1 2026 (Jan–Mar 2026):

- **Deep-subprime:** 3.85% → 4.24%, up 39 bps (+10.1%). This is the biggest increase in basis points.
- **Subprime:** 1.82% → 2.02%, up 21 bps (+11.3%).
- **Near-prime:** 0.63% → 0.66%, up 3 bps (+4.4%). This is the smallest relative increase.
- **Prime:** 0.17% → 0.19%, up 2 bps (+13.7%). This is the biggest relative increase, but from a very low starting point.

Losses rose more in the riskier tiers in basis points. Deep-subprime is still about 22 times Prime in Q1 2026.
sql:
WITH __ms AS (
  SELECT
    credit_tier,
    month_end,
    charge_off_rate
  FROM SNOWPACK_MACRO_STRESS.CORE.MACRO_STRESS_BENCHMARK
)
SELECT
  credit_tier,
  AVG(
    CASE
      WHEN month_end >= '2025-07-01' AND month_end < '2025-10-01'
      THEN charge_off_rate
    END
  ) AS q3_2025_charge_off,
  AVG(
    CASE
      WHEN month_end >= '2026-01-01' AND month_end < '2026-04-01'
      THEN charge_off_rate
    END
  ) AS q1_2026_charge_off,
  q1_2026_charge_off - q3_2025_charge_off AS change,
  (
    q1_2026_charge_off - q3_2025_charge_off
  ) / NULLIF(NULLIF(q3_2025_charge_off, 0), 0) AS pct_change
FROM __ms
WHERE
  month_end >= '2025-07-01' AND month_end < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY
  credit_tier
ORDER BY
  q1_2026_charge_off DESC NULLS LAST /* Generated by Cortex */;

tables.title: Avg Charge-off Rate by Credit Tier: Q3 2025 vs Q1 2026

question: What was the average charge-off rate by credit tier in Q1 2026 compared with Q3 2025?

text:
Two products, **Debit and Prepaid**, had zero charge-offs. Their charge-off rate was 0 in every tier and every month from July 2024 to June 2026, including June 2026. Together they carried about **47.7% of June 2026 volume**, roughly $2.40B of about $5.03B.

| Product | June 2026 volume | Share of June 2026 volume | Highest charge-off rate (Jul 2024–Jun 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debit | $1.74B | 34.6% | 0% |
| Prepaid | $0.66B | 13.1% | 0% |
| Credit card | $2.01B | 40.1% | 9.33% |
| BNPL | $0.61B | 12.2% | 10.08% |

Debit and prepaid don't extend credit, so their zero charge-offs probably reflect how the products work rather than better credit performance. That means all of the portfolio's charge-off risk sits in credit card and BNPL, which made up about 52.3% of June 2026 volume.
sql:
WITH __ms AS (
  SELECT
    month_end,
    product,
    charge_off_rate,
    transaction_volume_usd
  FROM SNOWPACK_MACRO_STRESS.CORE.MACRO_STRESS_BENCHMARK
), p AS (
  SELECT
    product,
    MAX(charge_off_rate) AS mx_all,
    MAX(
      CASE
        WHEN month_end >= '2026-06-01' AND month_end < '2026-07-01'
        THEN charge_off_rate
      END
    ) AS mx_jun,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN month_end >= '2026-06-01' AND month_end < '2026-07-01'
        THEN transaction_volume_usd
      END
    ) AS vol_jun,
    MIN(month_end) AS s,
    MAX(month_end) AS e
  FROM __ms
  GROUP BY
    product
)
SELECT
  product,
  mx_all,
  mx_jun,
  vol_jun,
  vol_jun / NULLIF(SUM(vol_jun) OVER (), 0) AS share_jun,
  s,
  e
FROM p
ORDER BY
  mx_all /* Generated by Cortex */;
